A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Locket research work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix C report original measurements of feature locking, utility, jailbreak resistance and scalability across three language models.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds larger-model, eight-feature, additional-comparator, runtime and stochastic-inference results in Section 7 and Appendices F–I.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 moves merging, clipping and adapter attachment from the per-request inference routine into a separate per-client routine; Section 7 specifies attachment once per session. The feature-specific adapters, adversarial training objective and spectral-norm merging rule remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The original datasets remain. Appendix I adds selective locking of Law, History, Psychology, Politics and Philosophy as separate MMLU-derived features, previously covered collectively by general knowledge. This introduces finer-grained authorization tasks among overlapping subdomains, without adding a new source dataset.

E2.justification: Table 12 adds an evaluated password-locking-plus-circuit-breaking comparator, PWD + CB. Table 8 substantially expands merging comparisons with SVD, TIES SVD, four DARE variants and two magnitude-pruning variants. The original PWD and Linear/CAT/TIES comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce 4-bit Llama-3-70B-Instruct, temperature-1 sampling, progressive locking up to eight features, and adapter attachment/detachment and time-to-first-token measurements. Table 8 reports averaged locked-feature accuracy alongside unlocked accuracy. Original data splits, training settings and main evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a stochastic-decoding robustness check in Appendix F, expands merging analysis to distinguish over-refusal from ineffective locking in Appendix G, and tests scalability and interference through eight-feature locking in Appendix I. The original clipping-threshold sensitivity plot and jailbreak analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-run uncertainty reporting. v2 adds runtime averages over five runs with ± values and ten independent temperature-1 inference runs with reported ±1% and ±2% variation. These additions are localized; the main result tables still lack uncertainty estimates, and the meaning of the ± quantities is unspecified.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial comparator, scalability, runtime and sampling results. Table 9 reveals incomplete locking in some configurations and Philosophy accuracy falling from 0.49 to 0.34 with seven features locked. Retained results also change: Table 4 swaps Llama Math's final two entries from 0.00/0.23 to 0.23/0.00; Table 5 updates Locket's MMLU score with M+Q locked from 0.51 to 0.53; v1 Table 8/v2 Table 10 changes locked Math from 0.92 to 0.00. Tables 2–3 are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The FLoTE mapping, loss expressions, perturbation optimization and spectral-norm formulas retain their mathematical substance. Naming the averaged refusal loss Lrobust and adding an informal feature definition clarify existing concepts; no new theorem, proof or substantive formal assumption appears.

C1.justification: The headline claims of 100% refusal, at most 7% utility degradation and at most 5% attack success remain. The introduction qualifies the contribution as the first method satisfying all four requirements within the evaluated setting and acknowledges that prior password-locking methods are not uniformly vulnerable to adversarial prompting.

C2.justification: v2 refines the existing interference discussion by distinguishing it from catastrophic forgetting and interpreting the eight-feature degradation as an overlap problem. It adds an economic-feasibility interpretation of runtime measurements and proposes overlap removal and vLLM serving as future mitigations. The warning about stronger future attacks is retained.

D1.justification: v2 specifies A100 40GB hardware, updates reported total computation from approximately 5,000 to 6,000 GPU hours, discloses adapter parameter counts and identifies PEFT as the source of additional merging implementations. The original training and attack hyperparameters move from Appendix B to E unchanged; the promise to release code upon publication remains.

R1.justification: Sections 2–3 add pay-to-unlock literature and substantially revise the assessment of prior defenses. Table 1 changes existing methods' utility-preservation ratings from satisfied to unsatisfied and naive-jailbreak resistance from unsatisfied to satisfied, while recognizing Hofstätter et al.'s circuit-breaking robustness. Additional citations cover circuit breakers, preference/adversarial training, PEFT and vLLM.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, problem statement and evaluation prose are extensively rewritten or condensed. Unlearning moves into the alternative-techniques discussion, applications move to Appendix D, and discussion/limitations topics are reorganized. The appendices expand from A–C to A–I with additional explanatory sections and analyses.

P2.justification: v2 adds full-width merging and eight-feature matrices in Tables 8–9 and separate PWD + CB and 70B comparisons in Tables 12–13. Table 1 gains a comparator row, Algorithm 1 gains a separate routine block, and several tables move. Original appendix Tables 8–9 become Tables 10–11. Both original figures retain identical graphics, with caption edits.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly left broader model coverage and scalability beyond four features unresolved. v2 substantially strengthens these central aspects through 70B and eight-feature evaluations, a stronger PWD + CB comparator, expanded merging comparisons, and runtime and stochastic-decoding checks. Updated table entries also improve consistency. The new experiments usefully expose locking and utility limitations, although the abstract's perfect-locking and 7% headline claims need clearer scope in light of those results, and uncertainty reporting remains limited.
